courseTitle: The USA, 1954–75: Conflict at Home & Abroad
disclaimer: Aligned to Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) History (1HI0). Independent educational resource — not endorsed by Pearson.
contextBoundaryNote: Earlier precedents such as Plessy v. Ferguson (1896), CORE founding (1942), and Executive Order 9981 (1948) explain the early 1950s position; Edexcel Option 33 strictly examines 1954–75.

root.label: USA: Civil Rights & Vietnam
root.gloss: Paper 3 Modern Depth Study examining domestic US civil rights struggles and American involvement in Vietnam from 1954 to 1975.

children.label: KT1: Civil Rights Movement
children.gloss: Key topic 1: The development of the civil rights movement, 1954–60 — early 1950s segregation, Brown and Little Rock, the Montgomery Bus Boycott, and white opposition.

children.label: 1.1 Position in Early 1950s
children.q3dDebate: Legalised Southern Jim Crow statutes & voter disenfranchisement vs economic dependency & vigilante terror; plus elite NAACP lawsuits vs CORE grassroots direct action.
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Legalised Southern Jim Crow statutes & voter disenfranchisement vs economic dependency & vigilante terror; plus elite NAACP lawsuits vs CORE grassroots direct action.

children.label: Southern Jim Crow Segregation
children.gloss: Seventeen Southern states and Washington D.C. enforced legal de jure segregation and daily racial discrimination across schools, transport, and courts.

children.label: 1896 Plessy Legal Shield
children.detail: The Supreme Court separate-but-equal precedent let Southern states enforce racial separation legally.
children.gloss: The Supreme Court separate-but-equal precedent let Southern states enforce racial separation legally.

children.label: 17 Segregated Southern States
children.detail: Black schools, hospitals, and buses received starved tax budgets while Northern cities kept de facto bias.
children.gloss: Black schools, hospitals, and buses received starved tax budgets while Northern cities kept de facto bias.

children.label: State Laws Locked In Inequality
children.detail: Binding Jim Crow statutes and all-white criminal juries gave legal immunity to Southern white supremacy.
children.gloss: Binding Jim Crow statutes and all-white criminal juries gave legal immunity to Southern white supremacy.

children.label: Sharecropper Poverty & Terror
children.detail: Tenant eviction threats, job sackings, and unpunished vigilante violence silenced daily Black protest.
children.gloss: Tenant eviction threats, job sackings, and unpunished vigilante violence silenced daily Black protest.

children.label: Southern Voting Rights Barriers
children.gloss: White registrars stripped Black citizens of voting rights in the Southern states through poll taxes, rigged literacy tests, and intimidation.

children.label: Poll Taxes & Literacy Traps
children.detail: Impoverished Black applicants faced cumulative fees and impossible constitutional tests from white registrars.
children.gloss: Impoverished Black applicants faced cumulative fees and impossible constitutional tests from white registrars.

children.label: Under 5% Mississippi Voters
children.detail: Grandfather clauses protected poor whites while Black registration stayed below five percent in Mississippi.
children.gloss: Grandfather clauses protected poor whites while Black registration stayed below five percent in Mississippi.

children.label: Disenfranchisement Blocked Reform
children.detail: Without votes, Black Southerners could not elect fair sheriffs, sit on juries, or repeal Jim Crow laws.
children.gloss: Without votes, Black Southerners could not elect fair sheriffs, sit on juries, or repeal Jim Crow laws.

children.label: Reprisals Backed Registrar Rules
children.detail: Cross-burnings, bank foreclosures, and sackings deterred Black voters even where legal loopholes failed.
children.gloss: Cross-burnings, bank foreclosures, and sackings deterred Black voters even where legal loopholes failed.

children.label: Work of NAACP & CORE
children.gloss: Early civil rights organisations including the NAACP and CORE challenged Southern discrimination through federal test cases and non-violent sit-ins.

children.label: WW2 Double V & Truman Order
children.detail: One million Black veterans and Executive Order 9981 (1948) raised expectations for domestic equality.
children.gloss: One million Black veterans and Executive Order 9981 (1948) raised expectations for domestic equality.

children.label: Marshall & 1947 Bus Ride
children.detail: Thurgood Marshall won Sweatt v. Painter (1950) while CORE staged the 1947 Journey of Reconciliation.
children.gloss: Thurgood Marshall won Sweatt v. Painter (1950) while CORE staged the 1947 Journey of Reconciliation.

children.label: NAACP Courts Cracked Plessy
children.detail: Fourteenth Amendment lawsuits by the Legal Defense Fund dismantled segregation where state politics was shut.
children.gloss: Fourteenth Amendment lawsuits by the Legal Defense Fund dismantled segregation where state politics was shut.

children.label: CORE Pioneered Direct Action
children.detail: Interracial sit-ins and bus rides showed courtroom victories needed grassroots protest to force compliance.
children.gloss: Interracial sit-ins and bus rides showed courtroom victories needed grassroots protest to force compliance.

children.label: 1.2 Education: Brown & Little Rock
children.q3dDebate: Brown v. Topeka & Eisenhower deploying the 101st Airborne at Little Rock as landmark federal breakthroughs vs hollow victories stalled by Massive Resistance and school closures.
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Brown v. Topeka & Eisenhower deploying the 101st Airborne at Little Rock as landmark federal breakthroughs vs hollow victories stalled by Massive Resistance and school closures.

children.label: Brown v. Topeka Case (1954)
children.gloss: In the Brown v. Topeka case (1954), Chief Justice Earl Warren ruled unanimously that segregated public schools were inherently unequal.

children.label: NAACP Class-Action & Doll Tests
children.detail: Thurgood Marshall combined five school lawsuits with Clark doll tests proving psychological harm to children.
children.gloss: Thurgood Marshall combined five school lawsuits with Clark doll tests proving psychological harm to children.

children.label: Unanimous 9–0 Warren Verdict
children.detail: On 17 May 1954, Earl Warren overturned Plessy in public education under the Fourteenth Amendment.
children.gloss: On 17 May 1954, Earl Warren overturned Plessy in public education under the Fourteenth Amendment.

children.label: Shattered Segregated Law
children.detail: Stripping Jim Crow of constitutional legitimacy inspired Black Southerners to mount wider civil rights protests.
children.gloss: Stripping Jim Crow of constitutional legitimacy inspired Black Southerners to mount wider civil rights protests.

children.label: Lacked Enforcement Mechanism
children.detail: Courtroom judges commanded no police force, leaving Deep South classrooms segregated in daily practice.
children.gloss: Courtroom judges commanded no police force, leaving Deep South classrooms segregated in daily practice.

children.label: Brown II & Southern Manifesto
children.gloss: Vague Brown II timing after the Topeka ruling emboldened Southern Massive Resistance and delayed classroom desegregation.

children.label: All Deliberate Speed Loophole
children.detail: May 1955 Brown II omitted fixed deadlines, letting hostile Southern school boards stall integration.
children.gloss: May 1955 Brown II omitted fixed deadlines, letting hostile Southern school boards stall integration.

children.label: 101 Signed Southern Manifesto
children.detail: Over 100 Southern congressmen condemned Brown in 1956, keeping Deep South integration below two percent.
children.gloss: Over 100 Southern congressmen condemned Brown in 1956, keeping Deep South integration below two percent.

children.label: Massive Resistance Halted Change
children.detail: Senator Harry Byrd and White Citizens Councils turned Supreme Court victory into years of bitter stalemate.
children.gloss: Senator Harry Byrd and White Citizens Councils turned Supreme Court victory into years of bitter stalemate.

children.label: Border States Began Integrating
children.detail: Hundreds of border-state school districts desegregated quietly while NAACP lawyers challenged Southern delays.
children.gloss: Hundreds of border-state school districts desegregated quietly while NAACP lawyers challenged Southern delays.

children.label: Little Rock High School (1957)
children.gloss: Events at Little Rock High School (1957) saw Governor Faubus block nine Black pupils until President Eisenhower sent federal paratroopers.

children.label: Faubus Guard & Cold War Shame
children.detail: Orval Faubus used Arkansas troops to block the Little Rock Nine as televised mobs shamed America abroad.
children.gloss: Orval Faubus used Arkansas troops to block the Little Rock Nine as televised mobs shamed America abroad.

children.label: 1,000 Airborne Troops Deployed
children.detail: Executive Order 10730 sent the 101st Airborne Division and federalised Arkansas guardsmen to escort students.
children.gloss: Executive Order 10730 sent the 101st Airborne Division and federalised Arkansas guardsmen to escort students.

children.label: Proved Federal Supremacy
children.detail: Presidential military force and Cooper v. Aaron (1958) showed state governors could not nullify federal law.
children.gloss: Presidential military force and Cooper v. Aaron (1958) showed state governors could not nullify federal law.

children.label: Faubus Shut Schools in 1958
children.detail: Closing all four Little Rock high schools for The Lost Year exposed fierce ongoing white defiance.
children.gloss: Closing all four Little Rock high schools for The Lost Year exposed fierce ongoing white defiance.

children.label: 1.3 Montgomery Boycott & Impact
children.q3dDebate: Martin Luther King Jr. & church-led SCLC leadership vs grassroots organisers (Rosa Parks, WPC, MIA carpools) & Supreme Court intervention in Browder v. Gayle.
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Martin Luther King Jr. & church-led SCLC leadership vs grassroots organisers (Rosa Parks, WPC, MIA carpools) & Supreme Court intervention in Browder v. Gayle.

children.label: Rosa Parks & Montgomery Boycott
children.gloss: Rosa Parks refusing to surrender her bus seat in December 1955 sparked the 381-day Montgomery Bus Boycott.

children.label: Parks Arrest & 35,000 Leaflets
children.detail: After James Blake had NAACP activist Parks arrested, Jo Ann Robinson printed 35,000 WPC boycott flyers.
children.gloss: After James Blake had NAACP activist Parks arrested, Jo Ann Robinson printed 35,000 WPC boycott flyers.

children.label: 300-Car Pool & 65% Fare Drop
children.detail: MIA volunteer carpools across 48 stations sustained Black commuters and slashed bus company revenue by 65%.
children.gloss: MIA volunteer carpools across 48 stations sustained Black commuters and slashed bus company revenue by 65%.

children.label: Grassroots Women Built Boycott
children.detail: Parks, Robinson, Black church funds, and thousands of daily walkers sustained 381 days of solidarity.
children.gloss: Parks, Robinson, Black church funds, and thousands of daily walkers sustained 381 days of solidarity.

children.label: Economic Boycott Alone Stalled
children.detail: City officials indicted drivers and refused concessions until federal judges struck down transit statutes.
children.gloss: City officials indicted drivers and refused concessions until federal judges struck down transit statutes.

children.label: Martin Luther King & the SCLC
children.gloss: Leadership and impact of Martin Luther King united Montgomery behind Christian non-violence and led to founding the SCLC in 1957.

children.label: Unifying Young MIA Spokesperson
children.detail: Aged twenty-six and free of local rivalries, King inspired thousands at Holt Street Baptist Church.
children.gloss: Aged twenty-six and free of local rivalries, King inspired thousands at Holt Street Baptist Church.

children.label: SCLC Founded in January 1957
children.detail: King and Ralph Abernathy united Southern Black ministers to coordinate non-violent campaigns region-wide.
children.gloss: King and Ralph Abernathy united Southern Black ministers to coordinate non-violent campaigns region-wide.

children.label: King Gave Moral National Voice
children.detail: Disciplined Christian love calmed angry crowds after home bombings and won sympathetic Northern media backing.
children.gloss: Disciplined Christian love calmed angry crowds after home bombings and won sympathetic Northern media backing.

children.label: Relied on Local Organisers
children.detail: E.D. Nixon, WPC activists, and NAACP lawyers created the protest platform that elevated King nationally.
children.gloss: E.D. Nixon, WPC activists, and NAACP lawyers created the protest platform that elevated King nationally.

children.label: Supreme Court & 1957 Rights Act
children.searchTerm: Browder v. Gayle Civil Rights Act 1957
children.gloss: Success of the boycott rested on the Supreme Court ruling in Browder v. Gayle (1956), followed by the Civil Rights Act (1957).

children.label: NAACP Filed Browder v. Gayle
children.detail: Bypassing biased Alabama courts, NAACP attorneys challenged municipal bus segregation under the 14th Amendment.
children.gloss: Bypassing biased Alabama courts, NAACP attorneys challenged municipal bus segregation under the 14th Amendment.

children.label: Buses Integrated Dec 1956
children.detail: Supreme Court judges upheld Browder in November 1956, forcing integrated Montgomery buses on 20 December.
children.gloss: Supreme Court judges upheld Browder in November 1956, forcing integrated Montgomery buses on 20 December.

children.label: Federal Law Sealed Victory
children.detail: Supreme Court injunctions beat city obstruction while the 1957 Act marked Congress’s first bill since 1875.
children.gloss: Supreme Court injunctions beat city obstruction while the 1957 Act marked Congress’s first bill since 1875.

children.label: 1957 Act Gutted by Senate
children.detail: White-jury trial amendments neutered the 1957 Civil Rights Act, adding under 3% to Black voter rolls.
children.gloss: White-jury trial amendments neutered the 1957 Civil Rights Act, adding under 3% to Black voter rolls.

children.label: 1.4 Opposition to Civil Rights
children.searchTerm: Ku Klux Klan Emmet Till Dixiecrats
children.q3dDebate: Respectable institutional resistance by White Citizens’ Councils & Southern ‘Dixiecrats’ vs violent Ku Klux Klan terror and the murder of Emmet Till.
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Respectable institutional resistance by White Citizens’ Councils & Southern ‘Dixiecrats’ vs violent Ku Klux Klan terror and the murder of Emmet Till.

children.label: Murder of Emmet Till (1955)
children.gloss: Brutal racial violence in Mississippi peaked with the murder of Emmet Till in 1955 and the rapid acquittal of his killers.

children.label: Open-Casket Funeral in Chicago
children.detail: Mamie Till-Mobley showed her fourteen-year-old son’s mutilated body to 50,000 mourners and Jet magazine.
children.gloss: Mamie Till-Mobley showed her fourteen-year-old son’s mutilated body to 50,000 mourners and Jet magazine.

children.label: 67-Minute All-White Acquittal
children.detail: Despite Moses Wright’s brave courtroom testimony, Roy Bryant and J.W. Milam walked free and confessed in Look.
children.gloss: Despite Moses Wright’s brave courtroom testimony, Roy Bryant and J.W. Milam walked free and confessed in Look.

children.label: Exposed Corrupt Jim Crow Courts
children.detail: Unpunished lynching terrorised Black Mississippians and showed local white juries would never convict killers.
children.gloss: Unpunished lynching terrorised Black Mississippians and showed local white juries would never convict killers.

children.label: Galvanised Civil Rights Youth
children.detail: Shocking Jet photographs backfired on segregationists by inspiring Rosa Parks and young SNCC activists.
children.gloss: Shocking Jet photographs backfired on segregationists by inspiring Rosa Parks and young SNCC activists.

children.label: Ku Klux Klan & Bombing Violence
children.gloss: Resurgent Ku Klux Klan paramilitaries used dynamite violence, beatings, and church bombings across the Deep South.

children.label: Fury Over Brown & Bus Boycott
children.detail: Court desegregation rulings drove militant Klansmen to terrorise NAACP branches and Black neighbourhoods.
children.gloss: Court desegregation rulings drove militant Klansmen to terrorise NAACP branches and Black neighbourhoods.

children.label: 50+ Blasts in Bombingham
children.detail: Klansmen bombed Fred Shuttlesworth’s home on Christmas Day 1956 while local police shielded suspects.
children.gloss: Klansmen bombed Fred Shuttlesworth’s home on Christmas Day 1956 while local police shielded suspects.

children.label: Vigilante Terror Silenced Areas
children.detail: Collusion between local sheriffs and night-riders crushed open NAACP activity across rural Deep South counties.
children.gloss: Collusion between local sheriffs and night-riders crushed open NAACP activity across rural Deep South counties.

children.label: Failed to Halt Black Resolve
children.detail: Ministers like Shuttlesworth and King refused to retreat, while Klan bombings alienated moderate opinion.
children.gloss: Ministers like Shuttlesworth and King refused to retreat, while Klan bombings alienated moderate opinion.

children.label: Dixiecrats & Citizens’ Councils
children.gloss: Opposition to desegregation in the South combined ‘Dixiecrats’ in Congress with founding White Citizens’ Councils across Southern towns.

children.label: Uptown Klan Economic Pressure
children.detail: Founded by Robert Patterson in July 1954, Citizens’ Councils fired, evicted, and denied credit to petitioners.
children.gloss: Founded by Robert Patterson in July 1954, Citizens’ Councils fired, evicted, and denied credit to petitioners.

children.label: 60,000 Members & 24h Filibuster
children.detail: Bankers and judges purged voter rolls while Dixiecrat Strom Thurmond filibustered the 1957 bill for 24 hours.
children.gloss: Bankers and judges purged voter rolls while Dixiecrat Strom Thurmond filibustered the 1957 bill for 24 hours.

children.label: Respectable Elites Blocked Laws
children.detail: Senior Southern Democrats chaired Senate committees and starved desegregation without provoking media outrage.
children.gloss: Senior Southern Democrats chaired Senate committees and starved desegregation without provoking media outrage.

children.label: Worked Hand-in-Glove With Fear
children.detail: Economic blacklists relied on underlying KKK violence whenever Black citizens defied council warnings.
children.gloss: Economic blacklists relied on underlying KKK violence whenever Black citizens defied council warnings.

children.label: KT2: Protest & Radicalism
children.gloss: Key topic 2: Protest, progress and radicalism, 1960–75 — sit-ins and Freedom Rides, 1963–65 civil rights legislation, Malcolm X and Black Power, and urban riots to 1975.

children.label: 2.1 Developments, 1960–62
children.q3dDebate: Youthful grassroots direct action (Greensboro sit-ins, SNCC, & CORE Freedom Riders) vs federal executive intervention by John and Robert Kennedy (ICC & James Meredith).
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Youthful grassroots direct action (Greensboro sit-ins, SNCC, & CORE Freedom Riders) vs federal executive intervention by John and Robert Kennedy (ICC & James Meredith).

children.label: Greensboro & Sit-In Movement
children.gloss: Greensboro and the sit-in movement revitalised peaceful protest in 1960 and inspired Ella Baker to guide the founding of SNCC.

children.label: Woolworth Lunch Counter Protest
children.detail: Four Black students in Greensboro sat peacefully at a white counter on 1 February 1960, sparking rapid copies.
children.gloss: Four Black students in Greensboro sat peacefully at a white counter on 1 February 1960, sparking rapid copies.

children.label: 100+ Cities & SNCC Founded
children.detail: Store boycotts integrated counters across 100+ cities by August 1960 while Ella Baker helped launch SNCC.
children.gloss: Store boycotts integrated counters across 100+ cities by August 1960 while Ella Baker helped launch SNCC.

children.label: Youth Mass Action Beat Lawsuits
children.detail: Low-cost student sit-ins disrupted downtown store profits far faster than slow NAACP courtroom appeals.
children.gloss: Low-cost student sit-ins disrupted downtown store profits far faster than slow NAACP courtroom appeals.

children.label: Needed Bail & Adult Networks
children.detail: Student protesters still relied on NAACP bail funds, Black church support, and sympathetic TV coverage.
children.gloss: Student protesters still relied on NAACP bail funds, Black church support, and sympathetic TV coverage.

children.label: Freedom Riders & Anniston Bomb
children.gloss: Interracial CORE Freedom Riders tested interstate bus desegregation, facing Ku Klux Klan violence and the Anniston bomb (1961).

children.label: Testing Boynton Bus Terminal Law
children.detail: Thirteen CORE activists rode south from Washington D.C. to expose non-enforcement of Boynton v. Virginia.
children.gloss: Thirteen CORE activists rode south from Washington D.C. to expose non-enforcement of Boynton v. Virginia.

children.label: Anniston Firebomb & 600 Marshals
children.detail: Klansmen firebombed a Greyhound bus at Anniston and beat riders in Montgomery, forcing RFK to send marshals.
children.gloss: Klansmen firebombed a Greyhound bus at Anniston and beat riders in Montgomery, forcing RFK to send marshals.

children.label: 400 Riders Forced Kennedy’s Hand
children.detail: Relentless SNCC and CORE volunteers filling Mississippi jails shamed Washington before Cold War summits.
children.gloss: Relentless SNCC and CORE volunteers filling Mississippi jails shamed Washington before Cold War summits.

children.label: ICC Federal Order Ended Signs
children.detail: Robert Kennedy’s September 1961 ICC directive legally enforced terminal integration from November 1961.
children.gloss: Robert Kennedy’s September 1961 ICC directive legally enforced terminal integration from November 1961.

children.label: The James Meredith Case (1962)
children.gloss: In the James Meredith case (1962), federal marshals and troops defeated deadly riots to integrate the University of Mississippi.

children.label: Governor Barnett Blocked Entry
children.detail: Despite a Supreme Court order backed by the NAACP, Governor Ross Barnett barred Air Force veteran Meredith.
children.gloss: Despite a Supreme Court order backed by the NAACP, Governor Ross Barnett barred Air Force veteran Meredith.

children.label: 500 Marshals & Federal Troops
children.detail: After Oxford campus mobs killed two people, President Kennedy sent thousands of soldiers to guard Meredith.
children.gloss: After Oxford campus mobs killed two people, President Kennedy sent thousands of soldiers to guard Meredith.

children.label: Executive Troops Upheld Courts
children.detail: Presidential military intervention ensured Meredith enrolled and graduated, breaking segregated state universities.
children.gloss: Presidential military intervention ensured Meredith enrolled and graduated, breaking segregated state universities.

children.label: Reactive Crisis Management Only
children.detail: Kennedy hesitated and bargained privately with Barnett until lethal mob violence left Washington no choice.
children.gloss: Kennedy hesitated and bargained privately with Barnett until lethal mob violence left Washington no choice.

children.label: 2.2 Peaceful Protests, 1963–65
children.searchTerm: Birmingham Washington Selma Civil Rights Act
children.q3dDebate: Martin Luther King & grassroots peaceful protests (Birmingham, Washington, Freedom Summer, Selma) vs Presidents Kennedy & Johnson steering landmark 1964–65 laws.
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Martin Luther King & grassroots peaceful protests (Birmingham, Washington, Freedom Summer, Selma) vs Presidents Kennedy & Johnson steering landmark 1964–65 laws.

children.label: 1963 Birmingham & Washington
children.searchTerm: Project C Bull Connor March on Washington
children.gloss: King and the peace marches of 1963 in Birmingham and Washington mobilised national moral support for federal civil rights reform.

children.label: Bull Connor Dogs & Fire Hoses
children.detail: Project C and the Children’s Crusade provoked televised police brutality in Birmingham that shocked JFK.
children.gloss: Project C and the Children’s Crusade provoked televised police brutality in Birmingham that shocked JFK.

children.label: 250,000 Hear I Have a Dream
children.detail: On 28 August 1963, Big Six leaders united 250,000 Black and white marchers before the Lincoln Memorial.
children.gloss: On 28 August 1963, Big Six leaders united 250,000 Black and white marchers before the Lincoln Memorial.

children.label: King & Peaceful Protest Set Agenda
children.detail: Calculated SCLC media strategy in Birmingham and interracial unity in Washington forced JFK to draft a bill.
children.gloss: Calculated SCLC media strategy in Birmingham and interracial unity in Washington forced JFK to draft a bill.

children.label: Marches Alone Could Not Pass Law
children.detail: Southern Democrats still stalled Kennedy’s civil rights bill inside Congressional committees throughout 1963.
children.gloss: Southern Democrats still stalled Kennedy’s civil rights bill inside Congressional committees throughout 1963.

children.label: Freedom Summer & 1964 Rights Act
children.gloss: Roles of Presidents Kennedy and Johnson secured passing the Civil Rights Act (1964), while Freedom Summer and the Mississippi murders exposed voting barriers.

children.label: LBJ Broke 54-Day Filibuster
children.detail: Harnessing grief after Kennedy’s assassination, Lyndon Johnson twisted Senate arms to sign the July 1964 Act.
children.gloss: Harnessing grief after Kennedy’s assassination, Lyndon Johnson twisted Senate arms to sign the July 1964 Act.

children.label: EEOC & 3 Mississippi Murders
children.detail: Public segregation ended and the EEOC formed, yet Klansmen murdered Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner in 1964.
children.gloss: Public segregation ended and the EEOC formed, yet Klansmen murdered Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner in 1964.

children.label: Presidential Skill Enacted Law
children.detail: Only Johnson’s Senate mastery turned Kennedy’s stalled proposal into binding nationwide legal desegregation.
children.gloss: Only Johnson’s Senate mastery turned Kennedy’s stalled proposal into binding nationwide legal desegregation.

children.label: SNCC Volunteers Exposed Gaps
children.detail: Deadly violence during Mississippi Freedom Summer proved the 1964 Act still left Black voters unprotected.
children.gloss: Deadly violence during Mississippi Freedom Summer proved the 1964 Act still left Black voters unprotected.

children.label: Selma & Voting Rights Act (1965)
children.searchTerm: Selma Bloody Sunday Voting Rights Act
children.gloss: Peaceful protest at Selma provoked televised brutality that enabled Johnson to pass the Voting Rights Act (1965).

children.label: Bloody Sunday on Pettus Bridge
children.detail: With only 2% of Selma Blacks registered, Alabama troopers clubbed and gassed 600 marchers on 7 March 1965.
children.gloss: With only 2% of Selma Blacks registered, Alabama troopers clubbed and gassed 600 marchers on 7 March 1965.

children.label: Federal Examiners & 60%+ Vote
children.detail: Signed on 6 August 1965, the Act scrapped literacy tests and pushed Southern Black registration past 60%.
children.gloss: Signed on 6 August 1965, the Act scrapped literacy tests and pushed Southern Black registration past 60%.

children.label: Grassroots Sacrifice Created Law
children.detail: Courageous Selma marchers under John Lewis and King generated the national outrage needed for federal action.
children.gloss: Courageous Selma marchers under John Lewis and King generated the national outrage needed for federal action.

children.label: LBJ Enforced Federal Supremacy
children.detail: Johnson’s We Shall Overcome address and federal voting registrars delivered lasting Southern political power.
children.gloss: Johnson’s We Shall Overcome address and federal voting registrars delivered lasting Southern political power.

children.label: 2.3 Malcolm X & Black Power
children.searchTerm: Malcolm X Black Muslims Black Panthers
children.q3dDebate: Black Power & militants fractured civil rights unity, alienated white allies, & drew FBI repression vs instilled Black pride & addressed Northern urban ghetto poverty.
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Black Power & militants fractured civil rights unity, alienated white allies, & drew FBI repression vs instilled Black pride & addressed Northern urban ghetto poverty.

children.label: Malcolm X & the Black Muslims
children.searchTerm: Malcolm X Black Muslims Nation of Islam
children.gloss: Malcolm X voiced urban anger through his involvement with the Black Muslims before his later change of attitude and 1965 assassination.

children.label: Northern Ghetto Anger & Self-Help
children.detail: With Elijah Muhammad’s Nation of Islam, Malcolm X rejected passive non-violence for armed self-defence.
children.gloss: With Elijah Muhammad’s Nation of Islam, Malcolm X rejected passive non-violence for armed self-defence.

children.label: Mecca Shift & Feb 1965 Murder
children.detail: After his 1964 Mecca pilgrimage, Malcolm embraced interracial brotherhood before rival gunmen killed him.
children.gloss: After his 1964 Mecca pilgrimage, Malcolm embraced interracial brotherhood before rival gunmen killed him.

children.label: Awakened Urban Black Dignity
children.detail: Articulating Northern slum frustration inspired Afrocentric pride, youth confidence, and Black Power.
children.gloss: Articulating Northern slum frustration inspired Afrocentric pride, youth confidence, and Black Power.

children.label: Separatism Alarmed Moderates
children.detail: Condemning white society and King’s marches alienated liberal donors without passing federal legislation.
children.gloss: Condemning white society and King’s marches alienated liberal donors without passing federal legislation.

children.label: Carmichael & 1968 Mexico Olympics
children.searchTerm: Stokely Carmichael Black Power Mexico Olympics
children.gloss: Emergence of Black Power saw Stokely Carmichael rally frustrated youth in 1966 and sprinters salute at the 1968 Mexico Olympics.

children.label: 1966 March Against Fear Split
children.detail: After James Meredith was shot in Mississippi, SNCC leader Carmichael chanted Black Power in Greenwood.
children.gloss: After James Meredith was shot in Mississippi, SNCC leader Carmichael chanted Black Power in Greenwood.

children.label: Smith & Carlos Podium Salute
children.detail: Barefoot 200m medallists Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised black-gloved fists on global TV in October 1968.
children.gloss: Barefoot 200m medallists Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised black-gloved fists on global TV in October 1968.

children.label: Global Symbol of Racial Pride
children.detail: Demanding political self-determination and cultural identity empowered young Black Americans worldwide.
children.gloss: Demanding political self-determination and cultural identity empowered young Black Americans worldwide.

children.label: Fractured Civil Rights Coalition
children.detail: Expelling white volunteers from SNCC and CORE split the movement and dried up mainstream financial support.
children.gloss: Expelling white volunteers from SNCC and CORE split the movement and dried up mainstream financial support.

children.label: Black Panther Movement
children.gloss: Founded in Oakland in 1966, the Black Panther movement combined armed police patrols with inner-city community survival achievements.

children.label: Newton, Seale & Ten-Point Plan
children.detail: Huey Newton and Bobby Seale formed armed citizen patrols in October 1966 to challenge police brutality.
children.gloss: Huey Newton and Bobby Seale formed armed citizen patrols in October 1966 to challenge police brutality.

children.label: Free Breakfasts & FBI COINTELPRO
children.detail: Survival clinics and children’s breakfasts served thousands before FBI raids killed Fred Hampton in 1969.
children.gloss: Survival clinics and children’s breakfasts served thousands before FBI raids killed Fred Hampton in 1969.

children.label: Practical Ghetto Welfare Aid
children.detail: Free breakfasts, health clinics, and legal aid tackled inner-city poverty neglected by municipal officials.
children.gloss: Free breakfasts, health clinics, and legal aid tackled inner-city poverty neglected by municipal officials.

children.label: Armed Shootouts Drew Crushing Raid
children.detail: Displaying rifles at Sacramento and deadly police clashes triggered J. Edgar Hoover’s COINTELPRO crackdown.
children.gloss: Displaying rifles at Sacramento and deadly police clashes triggered J. Edgar Hoover’s COINTELPRO crackdown.

children.label: 2.4 Civil Rights, 1965–75
children.searchTerm: Watts Detroit Kerner Report King Memphis
children.q3dDebate: Major legal & political gains by 1975 (end of Jim Crow, 1968 Fair Housing Act, Black mayors) vs persistent Northern de facto poverty, urban riots, & Kerner warnings.
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Major legal & political gains by 1975 (end of Jim Crow, 1968 Fair Housing Act, Black mayors) vs persistent Northern de facto poverty, urban riots, & Kerner warnings.

children.label: 1965–67 Riots & Kerner Report
children.gloss: Explosive urban riots of 1965–67 in Watts, Newark, and Detroit prompted the landmark Kerner Report (1968).

children.label: Police Brutality & Ghetto Poverty
children.detail: Southern voting laws left Northern slums, unemployment, and racist policing untouched, igniting Watts in 1965.
children.gloss: Southern voting laws left Northern slums, unemployment, and racist policing untouched, igniting Watts in 1965.

children.label: 34 Dead in Watts; 43 in Detroit

children.detail: Exhausting human and financial losses produced the Vietnam Syndrome and restored congressional war oversight.
children.gloss: Exhausting human and financial losses produced the Vietnam Syndrome and restored congressional war oversight.

children.label: 4.4 Reasons for US Failure
children.searchTerm: Strengths of North Vietnam failure of US tactics
children.q3dDebate: Strengths of North Vietnam (nationalism, Vietcong tactics, Ho Chi Minh Trail, Russian/Chinese aid) vs US military tactical flaws, Saigon corruption, & US domestic opposition.
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: Strengths of North Vietnam (nationalism, Vietcong tactics, Ho Chi Minh Trail, Russian/Chinese aid) vs US military tactical flaws, Saigon corruption, & US domestic opposition.

children.label: Strengths of North Vietnam & VC
children.searchTerm: Ho Chi Minh Trail Russian and Chinese support
children.gloss: Strengths of North Vietnam combined national devotion, Vietcong tactics, Russian and Chinese support, and the Ho Chi Minh Trail.

children.label: Anti-Colonial Reunification Will
children.detail: Fighting for national independence under Ho Chi Minh, communists absorbed over one million deaths undefeated.
children.gloss: Fighting for national independence under Ho Chi Minh, communists absorbed over one million deaths undefeated.

children.label: Soviet-Chinese Arms & Jungle Trail
children.detail: 30,000 porters kept Russian and Chinese rifles, rockets, and trucks moving south down the Ho Chi Minh Trail.
children.gloss: 30,000 porters kept Russian and Chinese rifles, rockets, and trucks moving south down the Ho Chi Minh Trail.

children.label: Primary Cause of US Defeat
children.detail: Resilient guerrilla ambushes, peasant endurance, and unbreakable supply lines outlasted a superpower.
children.gloss: Resilient guerrilla ambushes, peasant endurance, and unbreakable supply lines outlasted a superpower.

children.label: Could Not Defeat US Troops Direct
children.detail: Major offensives in 1968 and 1972 failed until American combat forces and air power withdrew completely.
children.gloss: Major offensives in 1968 and 1972 failed until American combat forces and air power withdrew completely.

children.label: US Armed Forces & Tactical Flaws
children.searchTerm: Weaknesses of the US armed forces failure of US tactics
children.gloss: Weaknesses of the US armed forces, corrupt Saigon allies, and failure of US tactics fatally undermined the war effort.

children.label: 12-Month Conscript Tour Turnover
children.detail: Inexperienced draftees rotated out just as they learned jungle warfare, breeding drug abuse and fragging.
children.gloss: Inexperienced draftees rotated out just as they learned jungle warfare, breeding drug abuse and fragging.

children.label: Free-Fire Zones & Saigon Collapse
children.detail: Napalm, Agent Orange, and Search and Destroy alienated villagers while corrupt Saigon fell on 30 April 1975.
children.gloss: Napalm, Agent Orange, and Search and Destroy alienated villagers while corrupt Saigon fell on 30 April 1975.

children.label: Conventional Firepower Backfired
children.detail: Fighting a political peasant insurgency with heavy bombing and corrupt juntas lost Vietnamese hearts and minds.
children.gloss: Fighting a political peasant insurgency with heavy bombing and corrupt juntas lost Vietnamese hearts and minds.

children.label: Won Nearly Every Major Battle
children.detail: US soldiers never lost a set-piece engagement, pointing instead to political limits and home-front withdrawal.
children.gloss: US soldiers never lost a set-piece engagement, pointing instead to political limits and home-front withdrawal.

children.label: Impact of Opposition in the USA
children.searchTerm: collapse of domestic consensus Vietnam Syndrome
children.gloss: Sustained impact of opposition to the war in the USA eroded presidential consensus, halted funding, and ended intervention.

children.label: TV Horrors, Drafts & Credibility
children.detail: Tet, My Lai, Kent State, and Pentagon Papers revelations shattered middle-class trust in White House war aims.
children.gloss: Tet, My Lai, Kent State, and Pentagon Papers revelations shattered middle-class trust in White House war aims.

children.label: LBJ Exit, Aid Cuts & Frequent Wind
children.detail: Anti-war pressure drove LBJ out, forced Nixon’s pullouts, and cut aid before Saigon’s 1975 helicopter evacuation.
children.gloss: Anti-war pressure drove LBJ out, forced Nixon’s pullouts, and cut aid before Saigon’s 1975 helicopter evacuation.

children.label: Lost Politically on Home Front
children.detail: Democratic presidents and Congress could not sustain a costly, televised war once domestic consensus collapsed.
children.gloss: Democratic presidents and Congress could not sustain a costly, televised war once domestic consensus collapsed.

children.label: Symptom of Battlefield Stalemate
children.detail: Domestic opposition grew only because Vietcong resilience and failing US tactics prevented military victory.
children.gloss: Domestic opposition grew only because Vietcong resilience and failing US tactics prevented military victory.
